title: Ex-Nvidia-turned-VC Amulya Vishwanath: ‘Physical AI is in its LEGO era’
slides: Why is physical AI stuck in its LEGO era?
Ex-Nvidia VC Amulya Vishwanath sees building blocks, not robots
Today's systems still need humans to snap the pieces together
Founders who design modular hardware now will lead
Pick one physical task and test modularity today
thread_text:
1. The LEGO era of AI

Physical AI today still needs humans to snap the pieces together — like LEGO bricks waiting for a builder, not autonomous robots.

2. Modularity is the missing piece

Ex-Nvidia VC Amulya Vishwanath sees building blocks, not robots: the winning approach is modular hardware that snaps together, not monolithic machines.

3. Founders who design modular hardware now will lead

Those who prioritize modularity today will define the next wave — because adaptability beats specialization when the environment changes.

4. Test modularity on one task

Pick a single physical task and try building a modular solution. If it doesn't snap together simply, you've found your bottleneck.

5. Your move: pick a task

Choose one physical task this week and prototype a modular approach. If it doesn't work, iterate — that's how you stay ahead.

instagram.caption:
Physical AI right now is LEGO bricks waiting for someone to snap them together — not robots running on their own.

Ex-Nvidia exec turned VC Amulya Vishwanath says today's systems still need humans to assemble the pieces. 🧱

He argues modular hardware, not monolithic machines, is what wins — because adaptability beats specialization when environments shift.

So founders building modular hardware now are the ones to watch.

If you're prototyping anything physical, pick one task this week and test whether a modular approach snaps together simply. If it doesn't, that's your bottleneck. 🔧
